findings.chapter: Cross-references (Ch 3 §3.8, Ch 5 §5.8, Ch 7 §7.1 vs Preface convention)
findings.evidence: Preface (p.19): "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." Violations: p.79 "unless we explicitly use expert offload/swapping (Ch 3 §3.6, Ch 18)"; p.141 "less the ~64 GB runtime reserve that Ch 7 §7.3 subtracts" and "matching Ch 4 §4.6"; p.161 "and Ch 4 §4.7 tags the same quantity the same way".
findings.issue: Four section cross-references use the exact form the book's own Preface convention prohibits (chapter number repeated after the chapter name: 'Ch N §N.M' instead of 'Ch N §M' or '§N.M'). The targets themselves exist and discuss the cited topics; only the reference form is malformed.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite 'Ch 3 §3.6'→'§3.6', 'Ch 7 §7.3'→'Ch 7 §3' (or '§7.3'), 'Ch 4 §4.6'→'Ch 4 §6' (or '§4.6'), 'Ch 4 §4.7'→'Ch 4 §7' (or '§4.7'), per the Preface rule; sweep the rest of the book (incl. Ch 8–26 and Appendix A, not verifiable in this round) for the same 'Ch N §N.M' pattern.

findings.evidence: Figure 3.4 caption states: "Resident weight... is ~94 GB... the always-on attention/shared block of ~1.4B ≈ 2.8 GB (1.4B × 2 bytes; the figure rounds that block to 3 GB)." and "the ~23 GB and the 25.6 GB are not competing [values]... Per-token read traffic... is 12.8B × 2 bytes = 25.6 GB". Table 3-2 row "FP16 active weight-read per token (batch-1 decode)" lists "~25.6 GB". Table 3-3 row "FP16 weight-read per token (batch-1 decode)" lists "~25.6 GB".
findings.issue: Cross-chapter inconsistency in arithmetic basis for MoE active weight read traffic. Ch. 3 consistently calculates the active weight read (~25.6 GB) using a 'component-derived' total of ~47B (implying ~1.4B always-on + ~45.6B experts), whereas the vendor-published Mixtral 8x7B configuration used for the KV cache calculation in the same chapter (32 layers, hidden 4096) implies a much smaller always-on block (~0.7B). If the vendor-spec geometry were applied to the weight read, the active traffic would be ~24.2 GB, not 25.6 GB. Ch. 3 mixes a '47B total' (which requires a larger embedding/projection layer than the 4096-hidden config supports) with a '4096-hidden' attention geometry, creating a phantom discrepancy in the active weight read baseline. The 'canonical' dense 70B uses a constructed geometry (8192 hidden) that is explicitly labeled as teaching, but the MoE example conflates the published 46.7B/12.9B totals with the published 4096-hidden config without reconciling the implied always-on size.
findings.fix_instruction: Explicitly state in the caption or Table 3-2 derivation that the ~25.6 GB active weight read is derived from the component-split (~1.4B always-on) required to reach the ~47B total, and note that this ~1.4B assumption is inconsistent with the published 4096-hidden architecture (which would imply ~0.7B always-on and ~24.2 GB active read). Flag this as a known modeling simplification in the 'Worked example, not reference' header.
